# OMP workers through Herdr

Use this dispatch adapter when Sol/OMP runs inside Herdr. Keep the [OMP roles, review guard and acceptance rules](./README.md), [planning loop](./planning-loop.md) and [implementation loop](./implementation-loop.md); Herdr manages worker terminals, not the development policy. T3 stays separate. Hermes is not required.

**Live status:** instructions prepared; OMP-to-Herdr worker dispatch has not yet been exercised. The authoring session was outside Herdr. The standalone OpenCode relay proof is not Herdr proof.

## 1. Establish the real caller

Before any Herdr inspection/control, check inherited context:

```bash
test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1
```

If this fails, stop Herdr operations and ask the human to launch OMP in a genuine Herdr shell pane. Never manufacture context with `export HERDR_ENV=1`, select the user's focused session from outside, or treat an ordinary terminal as a managed pane. Standalone OMP may use its existing routes; it must not silently substitute them for a requested Herdr run.

Inside Herdr, load the installed `herdr` skill, then discover actual syntax and live capability:

```bash
herdr --help
herdr agent
herdr pane
herdr status
herdr pane current --current
herdr agent list
herdr pane layout --pane "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Record inherited workspace/tab/pane context and the actual caller resolved by `--current`. IDs are opaque; parse responses, never derive IDs from examples or sidebar order. Confirm the coordinator remains `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol`, with authorized settings. Missing/ambiguous caller identity, unavailable agent kind or incompatible server stops dispatch; do not repair, upgrade or start a service automatically.

## 2. Start the selected worker

Use Herdr for reviewer **and** implementer dispatch in this mode, rather than invisible native tasks or standalone CLI relays. Reuse the session's authorized kind/provider/model/settings; verify supported kinds using `herdr agent` and native arguments using the selected runtime's installed help. Herdr kind is the CLI integration, not the model. No guessed OpenCode/MiniMax startup arguments and no unapproved model substitution.

Default to one sibling pane in the current tab, same checkout/cwd, preserving user focus. From caller geometry choose right for a wide pane or down for a narrow/tall pane. Example for the wide case:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Read the new ID from `.result.pane.pane_id`; verify the new pane is an available foreground shell at its prompt. Choose a unique live agent name. The following are **templates**, not ready-to-run commands; replace each angle-bracket value with discovered/authorized values:

```text
herdr agent start <unique-worker-name> --kind <supported-kind> --pane <returned-pane-id> -- <verified-native-model-and-agent-arguments>
herdr agent prompt <unique-worker-name> "<guarded task and unique request token>" --wait --timeout 120000
herdr agent get <unique-worker-name>
herdr agent read <unique-worker-name> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

`agent start` uses an existing pane; it does not create layout. Require actual readiness before prompting. Verify the worker's configured provider/model/settings match authorization and reviewers use their supported review/plan mode plus the exact OMP read-only guard. Do not guess equivalent permission flags. Keep prompts within the installed terminal/runtime's input limits; a rejected long submission is not permission to switch transports silently.

Before parallel starts, assign disjoint paths or approved separate checkouts and one integration owner; dispatch all independent reviewers before collecting results. Do not create new workspaces/tabs or choose a different cwd/checkout unless authorized. Children remain edit-only or read-only by role and skip all gates/formatters; Sol verifies.

## 3. Read, verify, and finish

Keep the name, returned pane IDs, request token, allowed paths, model/settings evidence, reports and timestamps in the task ledger. A successful prompt submission, settled `idle`/`done` state or terminal badge is not acceptance and may describe another turn. Require the matching complete report and actual owned turn/background-work completion, with no active child work; inspect files and run the coordinator checks required by the loops.

On timeout, `agent_prompt_stalled`, `blocked`, or `unknown`, inspect the same worker with `agent get` and `agent read` before any retry. Do not blindly resend. A wait timeout does not cancel work. If an approval/question is shown, ask the human rather than answer it automatically. Antigravity/Grok may look idle while background tasks remain active; obtain real completion evidence.

If a completed report is missing, first request more recent-unwrapped output. Only if that still cannot recover it, ask the same worker to save the report outside the repository and return its path. Read that file on the same machine; do not initially require file output merely to work around scrollback.

Preserve the coordinator, unrelated panes and user work. Clean up only owned workers/panes after completion and any unsaved work is preserved, using installed help for the correct termination/close commands. Never stop the Herdr server, close the session or kill unrelated processes. After pane moves, use the returned new pane ID or live agent name, not a stale ID.

## Live check still required

In a real Herdr shell pane at this repository, start OMP using the [existing Sol launch command](./README.md#start-directly). Ask Sol:

> Continue the authorized Herdr smoke from docs/plans/2026-10-20-omp-herdr-dispatch.md. Read docs/process/omp/herdr.md. Verify inherited caller context and installed support, then use one owned sibling pane for the selected OpenCode MiniMax reviewer. Submit a harmless read-only unique-token task, inspect the matching report and actual completion, preserve unrelated panes, and append evidence to docs/validation/omp-coordinator/2026-10-20/herdr-dispatch.md. Do not change product files, install anything, repair detection, substitute models or claim success if unsupported.

Until that succeeds, report **Herdr dispatch documented; live verification blocked**, not end-to-end support verified.

# OMP coordinator

OMP (Oh My Pi) is the alternative coordinator replacing Hermes. T3 Code remains active with its [own workflow](../planning-loop.md). Route by the application actually open: OMP uses this directory; T3 uses its existing process loops and council. Neither Hermes, Herdr, nor T3 is an OMP prerequisite. No installation, service, credential, proxy, or permanent OMP settings change is required by this workflow.

## Start directly

From the repository root:

```bash
omp --model openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol --thinking high --no-prewalk @docs/process/omp/README.md
```

Before planning or dispatch, inspect the active runtime's model/settings readback or session evidence: coordinator must be `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol`, thinking `high` unless explicitly authorized otherwise. Record requested and effective configured identity separately; a catalog entry or launch argument alone does not prove execution or upstream identity. Stop if Sol is unavailable or readback disagrees; never silently switch. This entry does not resume a session, invent a goal, run plan-yolo, invoke an advisor, or automatically transition to implementation. Take the user's concrete request into the [planning loop](./planning-loop.md), then the [implementation loop](./implementation-loop.md) only after authorization and freeze.

### When running inside Herdr

When inherited `HERDR_ENV=1` identifies a genuine Herdr-managed OMP pane, use the [Herdr worker dispatch adapter](./herdr.md) for both planning reviewers and implementation workers. Sol and these OMP loops stay in charge; Herdr supplies worker panes, startup, prompts, waits and readback. Do not silently use native tasks or standalone relays instead. Outside Herdr, retain the standalone routes below; if the user requests Herdr, stop Herdr operations and ask them to launch OMP there. Current Herdr dispatch is documented but **not yet live-verified**.

## Roles and session choices

- **Sol coordinates:** inspect sources, plan, dispatch, verify, judge, accept, commit, and deliver. Delegate product code and tests; Sol may make administrative documentation corrections. The current documentation migration explicitly authorizes Sol to author its process documents.
- **Implementers write; reviewers inspect:** neither reviews its own implementation, delegates further, commits, or pushes. Assign one coherent implementer or genuinely independent slices with explicit non-overlapping file ownership and an integration owner.
- **Workers are session-selected:** reuse the user's authorized runtime/model/settings choices and fallback. If missing, inspect the live available choices and ask once with risk-sized recommendations. No fixed implementer roster, silent defaults, or silent substitutes.
- Native tasks may use only actual catalog-supported models **and** an effective configured model/settings matching session authorization. The current task interface rejects explicit `model` for ordinary workers (`model is only accepted for seance`); do not fabricate that argument or treat an inherited default as the user's selection. If configuration cannot be verified, use a supported external CLI with an explicit selected model, or ask. Do not edit permanent settings to force a match.
- Record requested model/settings, configured readback, runtime/modes, and provider/session evidence when available for every participant. Mark upstream identity unverified unless independently established. Different provider labels do not prove family diversity. This migration's native documentation-author dispatch inherited configuration; requested Sol identity is not proof of that effective identity.

Assign paths before any shared-checkout dispatch. T3 and OMP must not write concurrently in the same checkout/branch: use separate checkouts/branches with explicit integration ownership. Isolation prevents collisions, not malicious access. Preserve all pre-existing user edits and untracked files.

## Review policy

Classify behavior, not file extension. Low risk means obvious low-impact typos/links/formatting: coordinator inspection and gates suffice. Normal work needs one independent reviewer at planning and final review. High risk (permissions, workflow contracts, compatibility, data formats, path resolution, exit codes, or load-bearing behavior) needs two independent reviewers at both stages unless the user explicitly authorizes an exception. Use fresh contexts and separate roles; for High risk require verified distinct model families, or disclose unverified identities and obtain explicit acceptance of the named pair. Current migration is High risk with the user's one-reviewer exception: `opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free`, default settings, fresh plan and final sessions. It is not a future default or waiver.

Every review brief includes risk/question, authorized scope, plan/reference or draft revision, exact diff base/tree fingerprint, named sources and gate logs, prior findings when applicable, and this **verbatim** guard:

```text
READ-ONLY CRITIC TASK. You are reviewing, not implementing.

Do NOT create, edit, move, delete or rename any file in the repository. Do NOT run
any command that writes: no formatters, no linters with --fix, no install, no
git commit/checkout/stash, no snapshot or golden regeneration, no test runs that
write into the checkout. Test output, if you need it, goes only to a temporary
directory outside the repository.

If you believe a change is required, do not make it. Report it instead.

Return only the report format below. Nothing else.
```

Require `EFFECTIVE_MODEL` (requested/configured/settings/modes/evidence; upstream verified or unverified), `VERDICT` (`pass | changes_required | unverified`), `BLOCKERS` (location, problem, expected behavior, evidence), `SUGGESTIONS`, `FILES_AT_RISK`, and `CONCEDED`. Implementers report effective-model evidence, outcome, files changed, tests added, checks **not run**, deviations, and blockers. Unsupported evidence stays unverified, never inferred from the requested model.

Capture `git status --porcelain` and SHA-256 fingerprints of scoped tracked/untracked files before and after every reviewer wave, accounting for additions/deletions. These detect changes; the guard and plan/read-only modes are **not a sandbox guarantee**. If files change unexpectedly, inspect, attribute, preserve user work, report, and stop. Never blindly restore. Respect actual runtime approval restrictions; do not bypass them.

## Dispatch and completion evidence

Use tools actually available in OMP, not T3-only orchestration APIs. Retain a ledger of brief, allowed paths/ownership, task/process/session IDs, selected/configured model/settings, start/end/status, complete result/report and evidence paths. For native children retain returned IDs and actual terminal status; for external tools retain process/session and result receipts. An idle terminal, completed turn, silence, timeout, or exit zero alone is not acceptance. Require a substantive report matching the assigned acceptance criteria and inspect the delivered files/evidence.

If delivery is uncertain, inspect the original task/process and result before doing anything else; do not blindly resend or launch duplicates. A wait timeout does not establish cancellation. Confirm terminal completion/cancellation and absence of active descendants before acceptance. Clean up owned terminals/processes and only owned unused checkouts after checking for user edits; do not kill unrelated work.

### Tested external OpenCode review route

OMP can invoke this through its bash tool; create a fresh brief and unique output directory outside the checkout for each review. The brief contains the guard and required report above. Example (replace the brief and unique output paths):

```bash
node "$HOME/.agents/skills/opencode-delegate/scripts/relay.mjs" \
  --brief /tmp/BRIEF.txt \
  --model opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free \
  --read-only --timeout 10m --out-dir /tmp/UNIQUE-DIR
```

This tested route launches OpenCode `run --model opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free --agent plan --format json`; installed OpenCode 2.0.32 supports `opencode models` without a provider positional argument. Do not add `--auto` or unsupported `--pure`. Inspect the external `/tmp/UNIQUE-DIR/result.json`: require `status: completed`, `exitCode: 0`, and read the **complete** `finalMessage` for an actual verdict and model evidence. Retain that report in the dated execution record; resolve its blockers before acceptance. Use a fresh session per round. Failure/unverified output is not a pass.

This exact alias is an external CLI route, not an OMP-native task catalog entry or an interchangeable OpenRouter route. The selected external reviewer route completed successfully; that does not prove all implementer/provider routes work or independently verify upstream identity. No OMP configuration change is required.

Collect all findings into one correction brief. Follow-ups are fresh independent tasks targeting changed areas and unresolved objections; broaden review if dependencies or acceptance change. Unchanged verdicts remain valid only for verified unchanged scope. After two non-convergent rounds, stop and escalate the disagreement/evidence/options to the user, rather than launch a third broad wave.

# OMP planning loop

Sol turns a concrete request into an authorized frozen contract. Follow the [OMP entry and role/review rules](./README.md); this is not the T3 workflow. Read [project-profile.md](../profiles/project-profile.md) for correctness and gates, and [machine-profile.md](../profiles/machine-profile.md) only for relevant environment facts, not T3-only APIs.

## Start prompt

```text
Act as OMP coordinator Sol (openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, thinking high).
Plan <concrete request>. Verify active configured identity; do not substitute.
Read AGENTS.md, relevant specification, sources, tests, and findings.
Follow docs/process/omp/planning-loop.md. Resolve requirements and blockers,
obtain risk-sized independent review, and freeze the authorized dated plan.
Do not begin implementation automatically.
```

## 1. Inspect before deciding

Read the request, `AGENTS.md` (especially sensitive-area findings), relevant specifications (`FULL_SCREEN_TUI.md` for TUI work), source/dependencies, tests, and snapshots. Record observed behavior, evidence, and unknowns. Inspect current checkout/status; preserve user work. Ask only about unresolved choices that change behavior; reuse existing concrete authorization.

## 2. Draft the contract

Write `docs/plans/<YYYY-MM-DD-slug>.md` with:

```markdown
# Plan: <name>
Status: Draft | Agreed
Authorization: <concrete user instruction, or pending>
Reference: <pending until freeze>
Surface: omp
Risk and review: <level, reason, independent questions, explicit exceptions>
Roster: <authorized runtimes/models/settings; requested vs configured evidence>
Expected child tasks: <plan reviewers + implementers + final reviewers>

## Outcome
Observable user result.
## Current state
Verified behavior, sources, baseline evidence, unknowns.
## Scope and boundaries
Allowed paths, exclusions, ownership and checkout isolation.
## Implementation steps
Coherent phases, interfaces, dependencies and integration owner.
## Acceptance
Behavior, meaningful edge cases/tests, four project gates and delivery authority.
## Review decisions
Findings, evidence, dispositions and reasons.
```

Use the [OMP risk policy](./README.md#review-policy): Normal one reviewer, High two unless explicitly excepted. Permissions/workflow documents can be High risk. Select workers/settings per session; no unavailable-model substitute. Keep scope sufficient to implement without invented requirements. Plan product access as read-only; tests use synthetic HOME, never the user's real application state. Inspect changed snapshot/golden evidence before any regeneration.

## 3. Review independently

First inspect draft fields, relative links, allowed paths, and source-backed claims. Prepare compact evidence-first briefs using the README's exact guard and report schema. Include one clear question per critic, relevant named sources, draft revision/fingerprint, and review criteria. Verify configured runtime/model/settings match authorization; disclose upstream identity limits.

Select the dispatch route before starting any critic: inside a genuine Herdr-managed OMP pane, follow the [Herdr adapter](./herdr.md) for worker startup, prompts, waits and report readback. Do not silently replace Herdr dispatch with native tasks or standalone relays. Outside Herdr, use the standalone route unless Herdr was requested; then ask for a genuine Herdr-pane continuation, without fabricating caller context.

Capture status/fingerprints, dispatch all required reviewers before waiting, and retain the README lifecycle ledger. Each round uses a fresh independent session, not a resumed author conversation. Inspect the complete reports and post-review fingerprints. Require a substantive verdict, not idle/exit-only success; unexpected edits trigger preserve/inspect/stop. Low risk needs no critic dispatch.

## 4. Resolve before freezing

Collect coordinator and reviewer findings into one decision list. Investigate concrete evidence; user-reported failures are ground truth, not a reason to rerun merely to confirm them. Record accepted findings and corrections, rejected findings with evidence, and deferred findings only when proved outside scope or non-blocking. No in-scope blocker can remain.

Use fresh targeted follow-ups for affected review questions, carrying the original brief and prior findings/responses. Broaden review when the contract changes; unchanged conclusions require verified unchanged scope. Two non-convergent rounds require user escalation, not a third broad wave. Set `Status: Agreed` only after requirements, authorization and required independent review are settled.

## 5. Freeze in two commits

Only Sol commits. A commit cannot include its own future hash:

1. Leave `Reference:` pending and commit **only** the agreed plan:
   ```bash
   git add docs/plans/<YYYY-MM-DD-slug>.md
   git commit -m "docs: freeze plan <slug>"
   git rev-parse HEAD
   ```
2. Put that exact **full** first-commit hash into `Reference:`. Commit only this provenance change:
   ```bash
   git add docs/plans/<YYYY-MM-DD-slug>.md
   git commit -m "docs: record plan <slug> frozen reference"
   ```

The second commit cannot change the operative contract. Commit presence is not human authorization. Push only under applicable user authorization; the current migration explicitly requires `git push origin main` for each commit and agreement of `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git rev-parse origin/main`, and `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`.

Before affected implementation, **both coordinator and implementer** inspect the referenced frozen version and confirm every approved operative amendment is included. Behavior, scope, compatibility, permissions, machine changes, or execution-contract amendments require explicit applicable authorization and a new two-commit freeze. Reuse authorization already covering the concrete action. An arbitrary newer plan commit cannot override the frozen reference.

Append-only execution records may log authorized roster choices, evidence and receipts; they cannot amend operative behavior. Finish with all reviewers terminal and owned resources cleaned up. Only after the freeze is verified and implementation authorized, proceed to the [OMP implementation loop](./implementation-loop.md).
docs/process/omp/implementation-loop.md:
# OMP implementation loop

Sol coordinates delivery of one authorized frozen phase. Product code/tests belong to session-selected implementers; Sol inspects, verifies, reviews, accepts and commits. Use the [OMP roles, review policy and lifecycle](./README.md), not T3 APIs. The current process-document migration explicitly permits Sol documentation authorship.

## Start prompt

```text
Act as OMP coordinator Sol (openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol, thinking high).
Implement <phase> from docs/plans/<dated-slug>.md @ <full frozen hash>.
Follow docs/process/omp/implementation-loop.md. Verify active identity,
authorization, operative amendments, checkout ownership and baseline evidence.
Delegate product code/tests to authorized session-selected implementers.
Children edit only and SKIP gates/formatters. Coordinate verification,
fresh independent review, acceptance and authorized commit/push yourself.
```

## 1. Establish contract and baseline

Inspect actual checkout/branch, current commit, and `git status --porcelain`; account for tracked and untracked user changes without overwriting or staging them. Use separate checkouts/branches if T3 and OMP will write concurrently; assign integration ownership. Never reset user work to get a clean baseline.

Verify authorization and the exact full `Reference:` using the [two-commit freeze](./planning-loop.md#5-freeze-in-two-commits). Both coordinator and implementer must inspect that frozen version and confirm all approved operative amendments are included. Later roster notes are not contract overrides.

The coordinator establishes these four baseline gates, from the project root:

```bash
uv run pytest --cov=skill_lens
uv run mypy
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
```

Reuse available session evidence only when the inspected tree, environment and commands are unchanged. Do not rerun unchanged evidence just to confirm it. Record baseline failures and resolve the authorization/scope decision before implementation; do not silently fix unrelated pre-existing failures. Product/application state is read-only: use synthetic HOME and isolated fixtures for tests, never real user configuration or data. Inspect changed snapshot/golden files and their cause **before** regeneration; regeneration is not a fix by itself.

## 2. Dispatch owned work

Prefer one coherent implementer for a phase. Parallelize only genuinely independent slices, each with explicit disjoint file ownership and shared interface contracts; appoint one integration owner. Never have apps/agents race on the same files or run parallel verification storms.

Each brief contains exact target/change, allowed paths, exclusions, source references, frozen plan/full hash, meaningful acceptance, ownership, and selected runtime/model/settings. Verify effective configured choices against authorization before dispatch; inherited native defaults do not establish the requested model (see [dispatch rules](./README.md#roles-and-session-choices)). Use a supported explicit-model external route when appropriate, or ask; never silently substitute.

Select the dispatch route before starting implementers or final reviewers: inside a genuine Herdr-managed OMP pane, use the [Herdr adapter](./herdr.md) for worker panes and lifecycle. Do not silently replace requested Herdr dispatch with native tasks or standalone relays. Outside Herdr, stop Herdr operations and ask for a genuine Herdr-pane continuation if that route was requested; ordinary standalone OMP remains available otherwise.

Children must **SKIP ALL tests, gates, linters, formatters and runtime checks**, including mid-flight smoke runs. They edit and report only; no review, delegation, staging, commits, push or settings changes. Sol owns smoke checks and all final verification. Their report must include effective-model evidence (requested/configured/upstream unverified as applicable), changed paths, tests added, checks not run, outcome, deviations and blockers.

Retain task/process/session IDs and result paths. Follow the README's uncertain-delivery, terminal-state and cleanup rules; no blind resend, duplicate workers, idle-terminal acceptance or exit-only acceptance. A scope conflict returns to Sol before expansion.

## 3. Inspect and verify as coordinator

After all assigned edits land, inspect the entire diff and actual files against the frozen contract, including consumers/dependencies. Account for untracked changes, enforce allowed paths, preserve unexpected edits and investigate attribution. Check relevant links, API examples, report fields, exact guard and source-backed claims. Inspect snapshot/golden changes rather than accepting passing assertions blindly.

Sol runs focused smoke/affected checks where useful, then the four gates above on the ready batch, with logs tied to the inspected tree and environment. Worker self-reports do not replace direct coordinator evidence. Do not repeat gates on unchanged valid evidence. If changes invalidate evidence, run affected smoke checks and establish all four gates on the final tree; no check is waived merely because the edit is documentation.

## 4. Review independently and correct

Use the plan's risk level and explicit exceptions: Normal one independent reviewer, High two, Low coordinator inspection/gates only. The current migration explicitly uses one selected OpenCode MiniMax reviewer at planning and one fresh final review. It does not change future policy.

Use fresh review sessions and the README's exact guard, report schema, fingerprints and actual completion checks. Supply frozen plan/full hash, exact diff base/current revision or uncommitted tree fingerprint, relevant files/dependencies and current gate logs through one complete evidence source. Verify requested/configured model/settings; disclose unverified upstream identity. Capture post-review fingerprints and preserve/inspect/stop on unexpected writes; read-only instructions are not sandbox enforcement.

Collect all findings into one correction brief. Sol may correct administrative documentation issues; product-code/test corrections go to the assigned implementer, still edit-only with no gates/formatters. Resolve every in-scope blocker with evidence. Defer only proved outside-scope issues or non-blocking suggestions. User-reported failures are ground truth, not something to rerun merely to confirm.

After corrections, update invalidated coordinator check evidence and request fresh targeted review from affected critics with the original brief, findings, responses and unresolved objections. Broaden review when dependencies, shared contracts or acceptance change. Verified unchanged scope may retain an unaffected verdict; no redundant broad review wave. Two non-convergent rounds require user escalation, not a third broad wave.

## 5. Handle amendments explicitly

| Situation | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation violates the agreed contract | Correct implementation. |
| Technical detail changes without changed behavior/boundaries | Record evidence; amend only if the execution contract changes. |
| Behavior, scope, compatibility, permissions, machine state or execution contract changes | Stop affected work, verify concrete user authorization, then use the planning loop's new two-commit freeze. |

Reuse authorization already covering the concrete action. Coordinator and implementer verify the amended frozen reference before affected edits. Append-only execution/roster evidence cannot silently change the contract.

## 6. Accept, commit and deliver

Only Sol accepts, stages, commits and pushes. Require all of:

- Every authorized acceptance criterion and operative amendment satisfied; final files inspected.
- Four passing gates with valid coordinator evidence for the final tree/environment.
- Required independent verdicts complete, every in-scope blocker resolved, and no unexpected reviewer edits.
- Allowed paths only; required docs/callers/tests updated; user work preserved and excluded from staging.
- Observed delivery agrees with implementer reports; every child/process terminal, no active descendants, owned terminal/process cleanup complete.

Record a receipt in the dated plan/execution record: expected versus actual launches (including failed/interrupted ones), corrections/reasons, requested/configured identities/settings and upstream limits, result/report/log paths, elapsed time and tokens if exposed (otherwise unavailable). Never equate prompt characters or task count with billed tokens or unmeasured savings.

Stage explicit allowed paths only, then commit:

```bash
git add <allowed paths>
git commit -m "<type>(<scope>): <summary>"
```

Push only as authorized. For the current migration the authorized destination is `git push origin main`; verify full hashes from `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git rev-parse origin/main`, and `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` agree. Report actual commit/push evidence, never assume delivery from an exit-only child receipt. Remove only owned unused checkouts after checking bindings and preserving user edits. Final receipt states what changed, why, actual checks/review evidence, commit/delivery status, deviations and any remaining user decision. Unchanged accepted evidence needs no duplicate verification wave.

# Plan: Herdr dispatch for the OMP coordinator

Status: Agreed
Authorization: User, 2026-10-20: “ok do this remaining small change”, accepting the proposed Herdr dispatch section plus a live check inside Herdr. Reuse this coordinator migration's explicit Sol documentation authorship and single OpenCode MiniMax reviewer selection.
Reference: 2656a6a1efb687b0d23c9679fdc2222cc18c07b0
Surface: omp; optional Herdr-managed execution; T3 remains active and unchanged.
Risk and review: High workflow amendment; existing user-authorized one-reviewer exception for this migration. Reviewer opencode/minimax-m3.1-flash-free, default settings, fresh plan/final sessions. Upstream identity remains unverified.
Expected child tasks: one plan review and one final review; Sol makes these small process-document edits directly. Native agent startup for the live smoke requires an inherited Herdr context.

## Outcome and current state

OMP inside Herdr uses Herdr for worker panes, agent startup, prompts, waits and report readback, while retaining the existing OMP planning/implementation policy. Standalone OMP retains its current dispatch routes. Hermes is not required. T3 is untouched.

Current main is 84162645f9114a16f745c14a179658783ce85cae. Only `.path` and the old 2026-10-19 coordinator draft are untracked; preserve both. This caller has empty HERDR_ENV, HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID, HERDR_TAB_ID and HERDR_PANE_ID. No live Herdr commands may be issued or environment context fabricated from this session. This is an actual blocker to the live check, not a reason to withhold reachable documentation work or claim success.

## Scope and implementation

Allowed: this plan; docs/process/omp/herdr.md (new adapter); narrow route/link insertions in docs/process/omp/README.md, planning-loop.md and implementation-loop.md; docs/validation/omp-coordinator/2026-10-20/herdr-dispatch.md plus herdr-plan-review.txt and herdr-final-review.txt. No T3 files, product code/tests, old evidence bodies, settings, auth, installs, services, proxy or Herdr session repair.

1. Review this bounded amendment with the existing selected MiniMax reviewer. Resolve blockers and perform the standard two-commit freeze; push each authorized commit to origin/main and verify full local/tracking/remote hash equality. Existing unchanged session gate evidence satisfies baseline; run all four gates after the edits.
2. Add a compact Herdr adapter based on the loaded installed `herdr` skill. Require inherited HERDR_ENV=1 and actual caller-pane readback; outside Herdr stop Herdr operations, never export fabricated context or target the focused session. Inside, learn current installed help/status and supported agent kinds before control. Retain Sol identity and existing role/guard/risk/file-ownership rules. No creation of workspaces, tabs or different checkouts unless separately authorized.
3. For worker dispatch default to a same-cwd sibling pane with --current/--no-focus and geometry chosen from caller layout. Parse returned opaque IDs. Start the session-selected supported agent kind and explicit authorized native model/agent arguments after --, learned from installed runtime help. No guessed MiniMax Herdr startup command. Wait for actual readiness, submit guarded named work through herdr agent prompt --wait with bounded timeout, inspect agent get/read, and retain uniquely bound substantive reports. Never substitute OMP-native tasks or hidden CLI relays for requested Herdr dispatch without asking. Retain fallback only when standalone or explicitly authorized.
